title: DiDi Pay in China for Foreigners (2026): Cards & Wallets
heading: DiDi Pay for Foreigners: How to Pay for DiDi in China
description: Foreign visitors can pay for DiDi using methods offered at checkout: an eligible card, Alipay or WeChat Pay. Check the ride receipt before paying again.
quickAnswer: Before booking, choose a payment method offered in your actual DiDi app or mini-program and finish its verification. After the ride, open that same trip record: paid, unpaid and bank-pending are different states. If the bank and trip disagree, stop repeated payment attempts and ask official in-app support to reconcile the trip before paying separately. An eligible foreign card or a wallet may work, but a saved card alone is not proof that a ride has been paid. Keep a backup for your next journey.

contentSections.title: Payment problem now? Match the trip and bank status
items: Open the booking in the app or mini-program used to order it, then compare its trip ID, final fare and payment state with your bank or wallet record. The states below are a decision checklist, not exact menu labels or a claim that we tested your app version.
A bank notification alone does not prove the ride is settled. If either record is unclear, ask official support to confirm the same trip before trying a second payment.

rows: Trip paid; bank charge pending
Keep the trip receipt. Do not pay the driver again for that fare. Ask your issuer about a pending entry that concerns you.
Trip remains paid; issuer confirms whether the entry settled or was released.
Trip unpaid; no completed bank or wallet payment
Check for a pending authorization first. If none is in progress, use an available method on that same trip payment screen.
The original trip changes to paid and you retain its payment record.
Trip unpaid; bank shows pending or completed payment
Stop repeated attempts. Ask in-app support to reconcile the trip and ask the issuer whether its entry is pending or settled.
Support confirms whether the original payment settled or whether another payment is needed.
Trip paid; two bank entries
Check whether both are settled, rather than one pending entry plus one final charge. If both settled, request a duplicate-charge review for the same trip.
Match each bank entry to its outcome; retain any support refund reference.
Driver requests a separate QR or cash payment
Show the trip status and use official in-app help to clarify any claimed unpaid fare or extra. A driver QR transfer may not settle the app booking.
The app booking is reconciled and any separate payment is documented.

contentSections.title: How DiDi Pay works for foreign visitors
items: The standalone DiDi app, a DiDi mini-program, and a ride-hailing entry inside another app can show different payment choices. Use the method displayed for the actual ride you are booking.

An eligible foreign card may be offered directly or may fund an Alipay or WeChat Pay wallet used in the ride flow. A card being saved successfully does not guarantee that every ride transaction will be approved.
Check the selected method before confirming the ride, keep mobile data available until the trip closes, and retain the completed trip record if a charge needs support.

DiDi's current official iPhone listing advertises international-card payment and English in-app support. It does not establish that every issuer, mini-program or ride product works. The payment options and terms displayed for your booking remain the practical check.

contentSections.title: Set up and test before the airport ride
items: Download the official app from your device's app store and sign in with a number that can receive verification codes.

On reliable Wi-Fi, add a payment method offered by your booking flow and finish issuer or wallet authentication. A saved card is only setup: it is not a successful purchase test. If you have not used it for a completed ride, treat it as untested and allow time for the official taxi queue.
Search for your hotel using its Chinese name or full address, and check the exact terminal pickup zone before requesting a ride.
At checkout, read the selected payment method, displayed estimate and applicable extras. Keep data access available until the trip is completed.

After arrival, return to that trip and verify its final fare and paid status, then compare with your payment record. Save the booking ID for official support; do not publish your full receipt or card details.

contentSections.title: If your payment is declined
items: First confirm whether the charge is pending or completed in both the ride app and your bank; an authorization hold can differ from a final charge.
If authentication fails, check mobile data, SMS access, card limits, expiry date and overseas transaction settings with your issuer.
Try another supported payment method within the same ride flow. Do not repeatedly tap pay if a transaction is still processing.

If the app shows an unpaid trip, use its support or payment screen and keep the trip ID. If a driver asks for an extra off-app payment, clarify whether the ride has already been charged before handing over money.
At an airport, use the staffed official taxi queue if your account cannot complete a ride; prepare your destination in Chinese and confirm how that taxi accepts payment.

contentSections.title: Know what the displayed price covers
items: A pre-ride estimate is not necessarily the final fare. Traffic, route, waiting time, tolls or the product terms may affect the charge shown in the completed trip.
Compare the ride ID, time, route and fee items in the receipt before raising a dispute.
Foreign-card currency conversion and issuer fees may appear separately on your bank statement.
Keep enough time and a second transport choice for a flight or train connection; resolving a declined card at the pickup area can take longer than expected.

contentSections.title: Resolve a charge with the right support team
items: Use the trip record in the same DiDi app or mini-program where you booked. Open its official help or customer-service route; do not switch booking platforms and assume the old trip will appear there.

For the trip or fare, tell support the trip ID, date and time, final fare, app payment state and whether the bank entry is pending or settled. Example: “My trip shows unpaid, but my bank shows a pending payment for this amount. Please confirm the payment status before I try again.” Replace these details only inside official support.

For a decline, authorization hold or bank settlement, contact the card issuer through its official app or the number on your card. Ask whether it sees an attempted transaction and what action it needs; a generic decline does not reveal the reason.

Keep redacted receipt and bank-entry evidence for the case. Do not send passwords, CVV, one-time codes or a full card number to a driver, a public post, or ChinaEase email. ChinaEase can help plan transport but cannot access or settle a DiDi payment dispute.

Follow the case outcome and recheck the original trip. No universal release or refund deadline is verified here; use the issuer and booking support instructions for your transaction. If you need to travel meanwhile, arrange another transport option without repeatedly retrying the disputed charge.

contentSections.title: First-trip checklist
items: Working phone number and mobile data or airport Wi-Fi.
Hotel name and street address in Chinese, including the correct airport terminal or railway station.
A primary payment method tested in the app plus a backup card, wallet or cash for an official taxi.
Vehicle plate and driver details matched to the ride record before entering the car.
Use in-app help for a lost item, charge discrepancy or an unresolved unpaid ride.

items: Source check: October 23, 2026. The official DiDi China iPhone listing supports international-card availability and English in-app service as advertised features; Visa directs cardholders to their issuer for account and transaction questions. These sources do not guarantee an individual payment, refund timing or a mini-program menu path.

This guide is a source-based planning and reconciliation checklist, not a report of a payment made on our phone. Actual screens, country and issuer acceptance, app version and refund handling still need transaction-specific confirmation. The status examples are illustrative, not customer cases.

faqs: Can foreigners use DiDi Pay with a foreign credit card?

Some account and ride flows offer eligible foreign cards directly or through a linked Alipay or WeChat Pay wallet. Confirm the payment options shown for your actual booking and complete any issuer verification before you travel.
Does a foreign card in Alipay guarantee DiDi payment?
No. The card, wallet, ride product and transaction must each be accepted. Check the selected method at ride checkout and prepare a backup.
Should I pay the driver in cash if my card is pending?
Check the trip's payment status and your bank first. Do not pay twice for one trip; resolve unclear charges through the ride app's support.
Why is the final DiDi fare higher than the estimate?
Check the trip receipt for traffic, waiting, tolls and product-specific charges, then contact in-app support if a line item looks wrong.
What if payment fails at the airport?
Switch to another method offered in the app or use the airport's official taxi queue. Keep the Chinese address and another usable payment method ready.
